subject: Cascade: subsidiary team expansion, rollout plan & renewal credit allocation
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <t.reynolds@cascadehealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-05-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Expanding to our regional subsidiaries — next steps and use of renewal credits

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the renewal walkthrough last week. We reviewed internally and two of our regional subsidiaries (Cascade North and Cascade Labs) are ready to onboard their product teams — roughly 6 additional apps total. Before we lock anything in with procurement, we need clarity on a couple of things:

- Can we apply the renewal credit you mentioned toward an addendum that covers additional API keys and a modest capacity uplift for peak hours?
- What is the typical lead time to provision new subaccounts / API keys for separate teams? We want staging and prod separation for each app.
- Any special steps for cross-account observability or a shared billing view (so central IT can monitor usage)?

Anna (cc'd) will coordinate procurement questions. Can we get a quick mutual action plan and an estimated timeline? Prefer a kickoff the week of 5/29 if possible.

Appreciate it —
Tom
Director of Platform Engineering
Cascade Health

> -Jasmine

Subject: Re: Expanding to our regional subsidiaries — next steps and use of renewal credits

Tom / Anna — thanks, happy to help. Quick summary and attached mutual action plan (MAP) to keep things tight: Cascade_Mutual_Action_Plan_v2.pdf attached.

High-level proposal:
- Scope: 6 new apps across two subsidiaries. Recommend provisioning one subaccount per subsidiary and one API key per app (6 keys). Staging/prod split: 2 keys per app (optional) — we can size based on traffic.
- Capacity: estimate a +20% baseline capacity uplift with burst headroom; Ben will confirm VM/GPU slot needs.
- Credits & terms: We can apply the agreed renewal credit as a one-time offset on the addendum that amends seat/api counts and committed capacity. Laura — can you confirm finance sign-off window for applying those credits to an amendment?
- Timeline: provisioning can begin once the addendum is signed; typical turnaround for subaccount and keys is 3 business days, SLA permitting.

Next steps I propose:
1) Review MAP and mark edits — Tom/Anna
2) Laura to confirm credit application and draft addendum — Laura
3) Technical kickoff with Ben to confirm capacity, auth flows, and monitoring — Ben
4) Sign addendum / provision keys / schedule training with developer enablement

Tentative kickoff week: 2028-05-29. If that works I'll send calendar invites for the kickoff and the technical deep-dive.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Reynolds <t.reynolds@cascadehealth.com>, Anna Park <anna.park@cascadehealth.com>

Date: 2028-05-24T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Expanding to our regional subsidiaries — next steps and use of renewal credits

Thanks — quick technical notes from my side (so the MAP matches what we can provision):

1) API keys / subaccounts
- We'll create two subaccounts under the Cascade master org (Cascade North, Cascade Labs). Each subaccount can have its own API key pool.
- For isolation I recommend 1 key per environment per app (staging/prod). For 6 apps that's 12 keys; if you prefer a single key per app we can do 6.

2) Rate limits & quotas
- Out of the box we'll apply per-key rate limits consistent with your current commit, but we can set per-key quotas for dev/staging to prevent noise.
- If you want burst windows for nightly batch jobs, we can add scheduled quota increases.

3) Observability and billing
- We can enable consolidated billing view for central IT and create role-based dashboards (token-level cost + latency). It requires a short IAM mapping doc; I've attached API_Key_Specs.xlsx with example role bindings.

4) Capacity sizing
- Based on the traffic numbers you shared in the renewal (avg 1200 rps across primary apps), adding these 6 apps with typical usage patterns suggests a +18–25% token volume increase. To be safe I'd recommend provisioning one additional GPU pool slot with an autoscale buffer.

5) Security & compliance
- No additional evidence is required beyond the SOC2 documents you've already exchanged. If any of the subsidiaries require on-prem/private deployment we should scope that separately.

I've attached the API_Key_Specs.xlsx sample mapping and a short checklist for provisioning. Happy to walk through this in the technical kickoff.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (650) 555-0178
